blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: The zoning base is rural: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019's schedule lists minimum lot areas of A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha and RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha depending on the zone text — the rural zones that cover most of this hillside. Its "89% single-detached" share is likewise UNVERIFIED.

Bare-land strata: none verified — count 0: The three strata complexes below are built strata on built lots, not bare-land strata, and must never be presented as lot stock. Where a bare-land strata lot did exist, the buyer would own the lot as a strata lot: strata fees and bylaws apply to the lot itself, and the purchase runs on a Form B (SPA s.

Assemblies / plan holds — documented as plans, never as inventory: (1) Urban Reserve: the OCP's Urban Reserve designation identifies lands the City holds for long-term future urban services and housing, and OCP policy states development of the Urban Reserve will not happen until specific triggers and milestones have been attained. 10.2.2, with subdivision below 2.0 ha restricted until the city population exceeds 100,000 and an area plan is adopted — was NOT confirmed in the OCP chapter read for the research: UNVERIFIED as to hectarage, section number and trigger wording. (2) North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan covers both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue (about 500 acres, per the City release) at this area's north side; it establishes future designations and does not itself approve construction.
ALR vs non-ALR split: the City describes farms and nurseries in Thornhill, but ALR status is per-parcel — no split figure is published, so none is stated.

Servicing: rural properties here may be on wells and septic — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained. Per-parcel servicing is UNCONFIRMED until the records for that parcel are pulled.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Thornhill

items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge, BC. The City describes Thornhill as a heavily forested, mainly residential area with several farms and nurseries, with a large mountain-biking and hiking trail network on 256 Street (17 trails, typically about an hour each). SnapStats lists "Thornhill" as a sub-area under Maple Ridge.

Main roads and commute: Dewdney Trunk Road and Lougheed Highway along the south side; 248, 256 and 264 Streets north–south; 100 Avenue and 112 Avenue east–west on the hillside. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Transit: route 748 (Thornhill / Haney Place) is a loop from Haney Place via 240 Street, McClure Drive, Jackson Road, 100 Avenue, 256 Street, 98 Avenue, 264 Street and 268 Street, weekday and Saturday trips only at wide intervals; route 701 runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road along the south side. No West Coast Express station in this sub-area.

Schools (Ministry-listed names/addresses only): Whonnock Elementary, 27471 112 Avenue; Albion Elementary, 10031 240 Street; Blue Mountain Elementary, 12453 248 Street; Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary, 10445 245 Street; Garibaldi Secondary, 24789 Dewdney Trunk Road. SD42 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12).

Recreation and services: the 256 Street trail network (City description in the first bullet); Kanaka Creek Regional Park at the west side; Whonnock Lake Park in Whonnock to the east. No recreation centre or library branch inside this sub-area — Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and Maple Ridge Public Library, 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in the Town Centre. No shopping centre inside Thornhill was verified on a City source: UNVERIFIED. Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street (24/7 emergency); Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 121 – 11900 Haney Place, 7 days, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Thornhill

items.t: Flood and hazards: the City's floodplain framework addresses flood risks from the Fraser River, the Alouette River system, steep creek watercourses and groundwater-related flooding. The City describes Thornhill as heavily forested; a City-documented wildfire interface map for specific Thornhill streets: UNVERIFIED. Parcel-level flood status: UNVERIFIED.

ALR block — full form (Thornhill farm/nursery ground): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Residence caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31.

Presales (REDMA) — Rydge units only: REDMA s. 21 gives a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging the disclosure statement, with deposits in trust under s. 18 — the frame for any unit still on a developer contract at Rydge.

items.t: The 249 Street parcels are labelled Thornhill but describe themselves as Albion. The Thornhill page's feed carries 249 Street land listings whose own text places them in Albion next to the Albion growth area — a buyer comping "Thornhill land" from the feed alone will mix two areas' ground, and which page owns the pocket is an open question in the research.

The bus that serves the hillside runs at wide intervals, weekdays and Saturdays only. Route 748's Thornhill loop is not a frequent-service corridor — acreage buyers here are driving; price the lot on today's service, not on any corridor plan (the adopted Lougheed corridor ends at 221 Street, west of here).

faq.q: What and where is Thornhill, Maple Ridge?
faq.a: Thornhill is a City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood and the board/Paragon sub-area name for the heavily forested, mainly residential hillside in east Maple Ridge, with farms and nurseries and a 17-trail mountain-biking and hiking network on 256 Street.

faq.q: How did Thornhill sell in September 2026?
faq.a: Quietly: detached recorded 13 active listings, 1 sold and an 8% sales ratio, while Condos & Townhomes recorded 8 listings and 0 solds, so no sales ratio applies to the attached split (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

The live page names Whonnock Elementary (27471 112 Avenue), Albion Elementary (10031 240 Street), Blue Mountain Elementary (12453 248 Street per the BC Ministry K-12 file), Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary (10445 245 Street) and Garibaldi Secondary (24789 Dewdney Trunk Road); catchments are address-specific — check any address in the SD42 School Locator.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Thornhill?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 13 houses listed with 1 sold in the month and 8 condos and townhomes listed with 0 sold in the month in Thornhill. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Thornhill a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 8%, a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: Are there any apartment condos in Thornhill?
faq.a: None verified. Every named attached complex verified here is a townhome complex on 248 Street; the rest of the sub-area is freehold acreage.

faq.q: How many townhouse complexes are there, and where?
faq.a: Three verified, all strata, all on 248 Street at the sub-area's southwest edge: The Terraces (10550 248 Street, built 2015, freehold strata), Terraces II (10480 248 Street, years 2017–2019 by unit, strata on the fresh listing basis) and Rydge (10640 248 Street, 61 townhomes, freehold strata, listings record built 2025).

faq.q: Is Rydge in Albion or Thornhill?
faq.a: Both claims exist in print: Raicon's own site and the presale record say Albion; its MLS listings say Thornhill MR.

faq.q: Terraces or Terraces II — are they one complex?
faq.a: The listing records treat them as two: The Terraces at 10550 248 Street (built 2015) and Terraces II at 10480 248 Street (listings record build years from 2017 to 2019 across its phases), though at least one listing at the 10480 address also uses "The Terraces." Confirm the strata plan number for the specific unit on the Form B rather than relying on the marketing name.

faq.q: Can I buy a bare building lot in Thornhill?
faq.a: There is no lot product to buy — no named bare-land subdivision offering, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering exists here. What trades is fee-simple acreage, farm parcels, Urban Reserve holds, and the 248 Street strata townhomes.

faq.q: Are The Terraces, Terraces II and Rydge land I can buy as lots?
faq.a: A purchase there is a strata-lot purchase with fees, bylaws and a Form B; Rydge additionally needs a per-unit developer-sale vs resale determination before GST/REDMA treatment is relied on.

faq.q: Is Rydge in Thornhill or Albion?
faq.a: Contested: the developer says Albion, the board listings say Thornhill MR. Price a 248 Street listing against the sub-area its listing actually sits in.

faq.q: What is the Thornhill Urban Reserve, in plain terms?
faq.a: OCP land held for long-term future urban services and housing; OCP policy holds its development until specific triggers and milestones are met — treat it as long-term, not imminent, and do not pay a near-term-development premium on the designation alone.
